title: Finite-Sample Wasserstein Error Bounds and Concentration Inequalities for Nonlinear Stochastic Approximation
summary: Stochastic approximation methods such as stochastic gradient descent and temporal-difference learning return either the last iterate or the Polyak--Ruppert average. We establish finite-sample Wasserstein-$p$ Gaussian approximation bounds for both outputs under a common framework combining moment bounds for the normalized iterates with quantitative Gaussian approximation of the appropriately weighted driving noise.
